sentence_stem: Had the committee been informed earlier,
correct_completion: the proposal would almost certainly have been approved.
full_sentence: Had the committee been informed earlier, the proposal would almost certainly have been approved.
acceptable_variants: the proposal would likely have passed without debate.
the outcome would almost certainly have been favourable.

options.why_wrong: This describes an unrelated event and does not complete the hypothetical result that the inverted 'Had ... been informed' clause introduces.
'So' presents a real cause-and-effect result, but the inverted 'Had' clause requires a hypothetical past outcome, so this does not fit.

options.text: the proposal would almost certainly have been approved.
the committee would inform everyone next time.
options.why_wrong: This shifts to a future habit, which breaks the past conditional structure set up by 'Had ... been informed'.

grammar_focus: Inverted third conditional (Had + subject + past participle)
explanation: The inverted form 'Had ... been informed' replaces 'If ... had been informed', so the main clause needs 'would have' followed by a past participle to express the hypothetical result.
translation: Se o comitê tivesse sido informado mais cedo, a proposta quase certamente teria sido aprovada.
